$comment: Every route and every MCP tool belongs to one capability. Checked by web/scripts/check-parity.mjs (part of npm run check).
agent: allowed        a person can do it in the interface and an agent can do it over MCP (rest and mcp both named)
agent-only     exists for agents; no interface route needed (mcp named)
gap            a person can do it, an agent cannot yet; a known parity gap with a note. The count may only go down (gapBudget)
closed         deliberately not for agents (the not_available_via_mcp list); every writing route must be session-only
infrastructure not a capability: sign-in flows, transport, public share pages, the SPA itself
wiki: the page that documents it. The check verifies the file exists.

pages.tree.summary: See the page tree and the templates

pages.read.summary: Read a page, its preview or its sub-tree as Markdown

pages.create.summary: Create a page or a database, optionally from a template

pages.update.summary: Change a page: content, title, icon, cover, tags, visibility, parent, workspace, favourite, row properties

pages.order.summary: Put sibling pages in a chosen order
pages.order.note: update_page moves a page under a parent but cannot set its position among siblings.

pages.favorites.list.note: update_page sets a favourite; list has no favorites kind to read them back.

pages.trash.summary: Move a page to the trash and bring it back

pages.duplicate.summary: Duplicate a page with its sub-tree

tags.color.note: workspace with workspace_id, tag and color; both doors call setTagColor (#2).

search.summary: Full-text search over pages and indexed PDFs

files.summary: Upload a file, attach it to a page, list files

collections.summary: Read and change a database: schema, views (charts among them), rows, and the counts and totals a chart shows
collections.note: A chart's numbers come from one function on both doors (POST …/aggregate, query_rows group_by). Saving a chart as a picture is drawn in the browser from those same numbers, so it has no route and no tool.

collections.templates.summary: A database's own templates: list, add, rename, remove, and create a row from one

forms.share.summary: Share a form view publicly so outsiders can submit rows

pages.share.summary: Turn a page's public link on or off

revisions.summary: A page's history: list, read and restore revisions

activity.log.summary: Read the activity log and revert an entry
activity.log.note: Agents have per-page revisions but not the workspace activity log or its revert.

comments.summary: List, add, resolve, reopen and delete comments

notes.write.summary: Add a line to a page's note trail

notes.read.note: Agents write the trail with note but no tool reads pageNotes back.

notes.clear.summary: Discard a page's whole note trail
notes.clear.reason: The trail is the record of what agents did; only a person may discard it.

import.content.summary: Import Markdown, CSV or a Notion/zip export
import.content.note: import_url imports JSON records from a URL; file imports are browser-only so far.

import.url.summary: Bulk-import records from a JSON URL and follow the job

export.all.summary: Export everything one can read as a zip
export.all.note: Agents read page by page with get_page; there is no bulk export.

workspaces.list.summary: List workspaces and read one with its members and rules

workspaces.manage.summary: Create a workspace, rename it, set its icon

workspaces.blueprints.summary: Start a workspace from the blueprint library
workspaces.blueprints.note: workspace from_workspace copies an existing workspace; the built-in library is browser-only.

workspaces.transfer.summary: Export a workspace as a portable file and import one
workspaces.transfer.note: Decide whether agents should move whole workspaces.

workspaces.delete.note: Not offered over MCP. Decide: closed (then session-only) or a tool.

workspaces.membership.summary: Add, change and remove workspace members and their roles
workspaces.membership.reason: Listed in not_available_via_mcp: workspace membership and roles.

tokenReachable.note: Decided in #1: no MCP tool, but a workspace admin's read-write token may manage that workspace's members over REST. README, whoami and wiki/agent-access.md say so.

workspaces.rules.summary: Write workspace rules for agents; agents may propose a draft
workspaces.rules.reason: Applying rules stays in the browser; agents submit drafts with propose_workspace_rules.

workspaces.rules.propose.summary: Propose workspace rules as a draft for an admin

workspaces.break-glass.summary: Owner access to a workspace in an emergency

agents.presence.summary: Announce work on a page and see who is working where

account.prefs.summary: Personal preferences, two-factor, calendar feed address
account.prefs.reason: Listed in not_available_via_mcp: two-factor settings; preferences belong to the person.

account.tokens.summary: API tokens and OAuth grants for agents

admin.users.summary: Create, change, disable and delete accounts; invitations; ownership
admin.users.reason: Listed in not_available_via_mcp: creating or deleting accounts.

admin.instance.summary: Instance settings, mail, tunnel, updates, webhooks, audit retention, the database's upgrade step and copies (spec 008)
admin.instance.reason: Listed in not_available_via_mcp: tunnel and instance settings.

infrastructure.auth.summary: Sign-in, sign-up, setup, OAuth for MCP clients, SSO and mail OAuth callbacks, desktop sign-in, invitation acceptance

infrastructure.transport.summary: Health, live events, presence feed, realtime editing, MCP endpoint, the agent skill bundle, uploaded files, the app itself, licences

infrastructure.public.summary: What outsiders see: shared pages, their files, public forms
